findings.title: Redirect-chain depth reduced from 10000 to 1000 without rationale
findings.body: The Lua script's redirect-following loop is reduced from `for i = 0, 10000 do` to `for i = 0, 1000 do`, and the original comment that acknowledged the limit ("theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") is silently deleted. With depth capped at 1000, any trace whose `span-buf:sr:` redirect chain is longer than 1000 will exit the loop before convergence, write the new span to a stale `set_span_id`, and then fail to merge subsequent spans into the real segment set. The downstream consequence is silently dropped spans (incomplete segments flushed out) - a data integrity regression. Either keep the previous limit (or document the new, lower bound), or actually change the algorithm so a depth-bounded walk is correct (e.g., iterate by current `set_span_id`, not by a fixed counter).

findings.title: Missing `end_timestamp_precise` will raise KeyError and poison the batch
findings.body: `process_batch` now reads `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]`. If any incoming span in the batch omits this field, the indexing raises `KeyError`, which propagates out of `RunTask` and causes the whole batch to fail repeatedly until the bad message is skipped. The existing pattern in this same function is to use `val.get(...)` for optional fields (`parent_span_id`, `is_remote`). `end_timestamp_precise` should either be sourced via `val.get("end_timestamp_precise", 0.0)` (or similar) or be guaranteed by the producer/Relay contract. Otherwise a single malformed Kafka message halts the consumer.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` allows negative offsets that Django ORM does not support
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features=True` and `cursor.offset < 0`, the paginator computes `start_offset = cursor.offset` and slices the queryset as `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django's QuerySet slicing with negative indices is not supported and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` (or, in some versions, produces invalid SQL `LIMIT -N`). The accompanying comment claims "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" - this is false. The new audit-log endpoint exposes this code path to any superuser or member with `has_global_access` (see `organization_auditlogs.py`), so any crafted `?cursor=...:-1:0` request against that endpoint will return a 500.

findings.title: Audit-log "advanced pagination" gated only by `has_global_access`, with misleading justification
findings.body: The condition `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is the only gate on `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`. `has_global_access` is granted to any org member with access to all teams in the organization, not just admins who should be exposed to a brand-new, untested paginator path. The inline comment "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" is also incorrect: the queryset is `AuditLogEntry.objects.filter(organization_id=organization.id)` with no per-row ACL, so the new paginator gives this broader set of users arbitrary row-jumping behavior (and, given the Django-negative-slice bug above, 500s on crafted cursors). Tighten the gate (e.g., only when `request.user.is_superuser`) and add an actual permission test before enabling advanced pagination.

findings.title: New `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is shipped with no tests
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is a 90+ line subclass of `BasePaginator` with new behavior (negative-offset slicing, `enable_advanced_features` constructor flag, duplicate `get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor` implementations copied from `Paginator`) but no test coverage is added in this PR. The `tests/` diff only touches the spans-buffer test files. Given the endpoint in `organization_auditlogs.py` already wires this paginator into production, this needs at minimum: (1) a test that exercises `enable_advanced_features=False` parity with `BasePaginator`, (2) a test of the `enable_advanced_features=True` negative-offset path (which will currently surface the Django negative-slice bug), and (3) tests covering `get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor`/cursor-string round-trip.

findings.title: Cursor constructor comment promises a behavior change that is not made
findings.body: The diff adds two comment lines to `Cursor.__init__` stating that negative offsets are now allowed for "advanced pagination scenarios", but the constructor itself is unchanged (`self.offset = int(offset)` was already there). At the same time, every other paginator (`OffsetPaginator`, `MergingOffsetPaginator`, `CombinedQuerysetPaginator`, `GenericOffsetPaginator`, `ChainPaginator`, `CallbackPaginator`) explicitly rejects negative offsets with `raise BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`. So `Cursor` accepts negative offsets but most paginators refuse them; only the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` uses them, and (per the finding above) it does so incorrectly. Either remove the misleading comment, or add the explicit validation in `Cursor.__init__` (and the new paginator) and propagate the relaxation to the other paginators consistently.
